_comment: Authored package-level metadata required by the pre-launch content gate: biblical genre (drives the genre-beat structure check) and verseContext (one sentence of narrative context for the key verse, shown on the Key Verse screen). Keep in sync with mobile/assets/stories/*.json via scripts/apply_story_metadata.py.

a-way-through-the-sea.verseContext: Moses says this to a terrified people caught between Pharaoh's army behind them and the sea in front of them, before God opens a path.

baby-moses-is-kept-safe.verseContext: This comes after long years of slavery in Egypt, at the moment a baby boy is lifted safely out of the river.

birth-of-jesus.verseContext: An angel says this to shepherds working through the night in the fields outside Bethlehem, on the night Jesus is born.

bread-in-the-wilderness.verseContext: God says this in the desert, when the rescued people have run out of food and are afraid they will starve.

daniel-and-the-lions.verseContext: Daniel calls this up out of the lions' den at sunrise, to a king who had stayed awake all night worrying about him.

david-the-shepherd-boy.verseContext: God says this to Samuel just as Samuel is about to anoint the tallest, oldest brother, while David is still out in the fields with the sheep.

deborah-leads-gods-people.verseContext: This is the opening line of the song Deborah sings after the battle, thanking God that the people gladly offered themselves.

gideons-tiny-army.verseContext: God says this to Gideon while Gideon is hiding in a winepress, certain he is the weakest man in the weakest family.

god-calls-abraham.verseContext: God says this to Abram in Haran, asking him to leave his country and his family for a land he has never seen.

god-calls-from-the-fire.verseContext: God says His own name to Moses from a burning bush, when Moses asks who he should tell the people has sent him.

god-lives-with-his-people.verseContext: God gives this instruction at Mount Sinai, asking the rescued people to build a tent so He can live right in the middle of their camp.

god-made-everything.verseContext: This is the very first sentence of the Bible, spoken when there is nothing at all yet except God.

god-made-me.verseContext: David sings this in a song about God knowing him completely, even while he was still being made.

god-promises-a-rescuer.verseContext: God says this to the snake in the garden, moments after the first man and woman disobey — the very first promise of a rescuer.

god-provides-a-lamb.verseContext: Abraham answers his son Isaac with this while they climb the mountain together, carrying fire and wood but no lamb.

gods-good-commands.verseContext: God begins the Ten Commandments with this — telling His people who He is and what He has already done for them before He asks anything of them.

how-to-pray.verseContext: Jesus says this on a hillside, teaching a crowd to talk with God simply instead of with long, showy words.

jacob-learns-grace.verseContext: God says this to Jacob in a dream, on the night Jacob is running away alone after tricking his father and his brother.

jesus-loves-children.verseContext: Jesus says this when His own friends try to turn away the parents who are bringing their children to Him.

jesus-saves.verseContext: Angels say this to the women who came to Jesus' tomb early on Sunday morning expecting to find His body.

jonah-and-the-big-fish.verseContext: Jonah prays this from inside the great fish, after running away from God as fast as a ship could carry him.

joseph-and-his-brothers.verseContext: Joseph says this to his brothers many years after they sold him, once he is the one holding all the power over them.

joseph-forgives-his-family.verseContext: Joseph says this to his frightened brothers after their father dies, when they are certain he will finally take revenge.

joshua-and-the-walls.verseContext: God says this to Joshua as he takes over from Moses, facing a walled city and a job that feels far too big for him.

let-my-people-go.verseContext: God makes this promise to Moses after Pharaoh has refused him and the people's work has only become harder.

noahs-big-boat.verseContext: This is the Bible's summary of Noah, who built an enormous boat on dry land for years before a single drop of rain fell.

noahs-rainbow-promise.verseContext: God says this as Noah's family steps out onto dry ground after the flood and sees the first rainbow.

ruth-finds-a-home.verseContext: Ruth says this on the road out of Moab, refusing to leave Naomi even though going with her means being poor and a stranger.

samuel-listens-to-god.verseContext: Young Samuel says this the fourth time God calls his name in the night, once Eli has taught him how to answer.

saul-the-king.verseContext: Samuel says this to King Saul, who disobeyed God and then brought God a gift to try to make up for it.

stars-in-the-sky.verseContext: This comes right after God takes childless Abram outside into the night and asks him to try counting the stars.

the-first-family.verseContext: God says this in the garden, looking at the one thing in a finished and very good world that is not good yet.

the-good-neighbour.verseContext: Jesus says this at the end of the story, to a man who had asked Him to name exactly who counts as a neighbour.

the-good-shepherd.verseContext: Jesus says this about Himself to a crowd arguing over who He is, using the picture of a shepherd who knows every single sheep by name.

the-lost-sheep.verseContext: Jesus tells this story to religious leaders who are complaining that He spends His time with the wrong kind of people.

the-lost-son.verseContext: This is the turning point of Jesus' story, while the son who wasted everything is still a long way from home.

the-passover-lamb.verseContext: God gives this instruction on the last night in Egypt, telling every family to mark their doorway with the blood of a lamb.

the-promised-son.verseContext: God asks this after Sarah laughs quietly to herself at the idea of having a baby when she is ninety years old.

the-tall-tower.verseContext: This wisdom saying names what went wrong at Babel, where people built a tower to make themselves famous.

the-very-sad-choice.verseContext: Paul writes this to explain what began in the garden — that first wrong choice is now everyone's story.

twelve-spies.verseContext: Moses prays God's own words back to Him at the edge of the promised land, after the people believed ten frightened spies instead of God.

two-brothers.verseContext: God says this to Cain as a warning, while Cain is still only angry and before he has done anything to his brother.
